+*UPDATE (09.10)*+

Follow-up Qs received from the PDPS today, with a deadline of 14 October. PDPS is asking for:

{quote}* _What was the password policy for fleet managers prior to the incident;_
* _What is the password policy for fleet managers after the incident;_
* _Had Bolt integrated two-factor authentication for fleet managers, would it have been possible to prevent the incident;_
* _Why does Bolt not have two-factor authentication enabled for fleet managers;_
* _In your letter of 28 July 2025, you stated the following:_
_“The attackers gained access to the fleet portal by reusing stolen authentication data, which they obtained through an Infostealer-type program downloaded onto the personal devices of fleet managers.”_
_If available, please provide evidence confirming that the theft of authentication data indeed occurred via an Infostealer-type program downloaded to a fleet manager’s phone (or, alternatively, provide an explanation of what supports this conclusion)._{quote}

We have asked for an extension until Friday 24 October.

+*THOUGHTS*+

* Password policy Qs:
** (i) Unclear exactly what PDPS means by this, but presumably it is: (a) what password requirements Bolt sets for FMs; and (b) whether Bolt takes any security measures towards protecting FM passwords.
*** Password requirements:
**** +External articles+: Based on driver requirements ([link|https://bolt.eu/en-ge/driver/guide/faq/]), password must contain at least 10 characters, start with a capital letter and must contain a number. I cannot see any other obvious public articles on this.
**** +IS Code of Practice+: ([Link|https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/]) 7.3(b): “_you shall have policies and/or guidelines for the strength and rotation of access credentials, e.g…. Prohibiting and preventing the use of default or weak passwords… Securely handling and delivering credentials (such as user name and password)_”.
**** +T&Cs+: ([Link|https://bolt.eu/ka-ge/legal/tnc-drivers/?category=rides]) Silent on password requirements.
**** +Internal policies+: We have a Password Policy ([link|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/4621435719/Information+security+policies]), last revised in April 2025 by Tarmo, but it applies to Bolt employees.
**** +General measures+: We have various other policies ([link|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/4621435719/Information+security+policies]), including access control policy, data classification policy, data encryption policy.
*** We should point out that passwords are largely at the FM’s own risk. It is their responsibility to set a password that is not easily hackable.
** (ii) *This has not changed since the incident*.
*** Mitigation measures status summarised in [this|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C091XE0RF1B/p1757493466097819] thread.
**** _(Detection) Implement security email notifications on new logins for the Fleet Portal. This measure is designed to provide timely alerts to account holders and support proactive containment in case of unauthorised activity._ - This has been implemented.
**** _(Detection) Extend/improve the access to sign-in logs for the information security team. This will provide the information security team with a comprehensive view of user activity and support the detection of a broader range of potential compromises._ - This has been improved.
*** As a general point - It seems likely that the strength of FM passwords had nothing to do with what caused the incident; rather, the FM devices got hacked, and the passwords were lifted off of them. As such, this topic is not strictly relevant - why would we need to update the password policy?
* 2FA Qs:
** (i) We need to check this with InfoSec - if the hacker had access to the FM’s email account as a result of the incident, then no (2FA would not have made a difference). If all that the hacker stole was username and password, then yes (2FA may have made a difference). 
*** Ultimately, however, it is impossible for us to say for certainty whether this event would or would not have happened if 2FA had been enabled - this is conjecture.
** (ii) The truth is this just has not yet been prioritised.
*** We definitely have not implemented this yet.
**** Max and Andres discussed how 2FA is expensive (both mandatory and voluntary) and requires a large tech effort ([link|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C091XE0RF1B/p1750421920288379?thread_ts=1750409161.432469&cid=C091XE0RF1B]). We do use phone OTP with an environment-specific password as a second factor, but not the other way around.
*** See responses to Q1 and Q4 on the AKI response ([link|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_VhWXipS8KM4XBdODEbbhP_4-_oezljr-Dr6A7Ve9Zg/edit?tab=t.0])
**** “_Bolt is committed to progressively adopting more secure authentication methods, including Passkeys, Social logins, and WhatsApp verification. Our approach prioritizes enhancing security while ensuring a user-friendly and inclusive experience for all customers._”
**** “_Users are currently authenticated solely through an SMS OTP code during sign-up. We are actively addressing this and are developing a robust MFA system. Our enhanced approach will incorporate a combination of SMS and email as secondary authentication factors. Additionally, returning users (i.e. users that have already signed up on Bolt’s platform using an SMS OTP code) are given the flexibility to authenticate using passkeys or third-party social logins (Google, Apple)._”
**** “_We also maintain comprehensive logging and auditing processes to identify and address unusual activity swiftly. We continuously evaluate and enhance our risk mitigation strategies. We maintain a Supplier Code of Practice and collaborate with trusted suppliers to ensure robust incident response measures and the highest level of data security._”
**** “_While SMS OTP is often used as a second factor within multi-factor authentication schemes, in the Bolt ride-hailing application it is currently used as the only factor of authentication. Bolt plans to implement voluntary multi-factor authentication (MFA) using email OTP as an additional security measure. Once activated, users will no longer be able to log in solely using the SMS OTP; they will also need to provide a code sent to the email connected to their Bolt account._”
**** “_This approach enhances security by requiring access to both the user’s SMS and email inbox, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access. Mandatory MFA is not currently planned to maintain user accessibility and a frictionless experience_”
*** NB. +IS Code of Practice+: ([Link|https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/]) Clause 7.3(e): “_As part of software development, two-factor authentication shall be implemented based on threat analysis. In the case of administrative remote access to an environment with Bolt-related data, two-factor authentication is always required_.”
* Evidence re Infostealer program:
** What I have seen already:
*** We do not have internal logs or anomalous activity on our own systems to flag the breach. Hackers used legitimate login credentials - because the access was authenticated, Bolt’s systems allowed the hacker to log in the normal way.
*** In the original notification, we said that “_The root cause presumably is that the breach resulted from malware installed on a few FMs' devices… Attackers accessed the Fleet Portal by reusing stolen credentials harvested via infostealer malware installed on the personal devices_”.
*** We have not identified the specific individual(s) responsible for unauthorised access to the data, given that they have taken deliberate steps to avoid detection. “_All the known victim accounts were accessed via mass login from few IPs (e.g. IP in sweden accessing 150+ FM accounts registered across 20+ countries within 10 minute window)_” ([link|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C091XE0RF1B/p1757507791115709?thread_ts=1757493466.097819&cid=C091XE0RF1B])
*** Alon asked this Q to Andres. Andres responded: “_Just to be 100% clear on this. - We have no confirmed cases of infection. This is strong assumption by the infosec team. Based on our domain knowledge and similar incidents within Bolt and elsewhere indicate that infostealer type of malware would be the most likely cause for this breach. In theory large scale phishing attack could be used to achieve same results, but it seems unlikely as we have not received any reports about such campaigns targeting fleet managers (at this scale we would expect at least some of the targets to detect and report the attempts). In addition the suspicious logins we detected might not be the only ones as threat actors operating infostealers can (and do) resell the credentials their malware has stolen._” ([link|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C091XE0RF1B/p1750838953471749?thread_ts=1750687936.218379&cid=C091XE0RF1B])
*** Andres also said the following: The general chain of our analysis shows that:
**** _It is unlikely that our internal systems have been breached or that Bolt insider has stolen and is selling this data -> No evidence of large scale exports from admin, sample data shown in dark-web is consistent with what is available via CSV exports from Fleet portal._
**** _We have recorded suspicious logins to a large number of unrelated fleets from a suspicious IP address in a very unreasonable time-span. -> This indicates that passwords are known to a bad actor(s)._
**** _These passwords can not be viewed from Admin-Panel -> While I think it would be possible for Bolt insider to change password, it would leave an audit trail and  be noticeable to fleet managers. As such the password disclosure had to happen off our platform._
**** _Common vectors for password disclosure at this scale:_
****# _Database breach -> based on the evidence we have, considered highly unlikely. There would not need to be logins to FO accounts from suspicious IPs, as the data would already be readily available. + passwords are stored in salted+hashed format that would have to be brute-forced to get the plain-text value which would be inefficient._
****# _Large scale phishing campaign -> Theoretically possible, but with 350+ Fleet Managers compromised the number of targeted accounts would have to be significantly higher as success ratio is not 100%. We would have expected at least some of the targets to detect it and report it to us._
****# _Malware on victims' computers -> Most likely scenario. This could disclose all the passwords stored in browsers' local storage which could then be used to login with leaked credentials (as we lack 2fa). These passwords also seem to be sold_
**** _We have also received a bug bounty report claiming 2000+ publicly leaked credentials belonging to Fleet Managers._
** In other words, we do not have hard evidence - it is just the most likely scenario.

Let me include my understanding below:

# Noot won the B2G contract with the municipality
# They are using their current supply and current (official) subcontractors to address the needs (SLA) of that contract → secured supply.

# They have signed the Bolt Business conditions as if they were an enterprise using our B2B services.
## NOTE: i) we are not a subcontractor nor have a back to back contract with them, ii) we are not bound by the same legal conditions nor have accepted liabilities (have we?)
# Why is Noot sending us a trip? 
## my understanding is that they are avoiding (as much as possible) being penalised by not fulfilling a trip, therefore, we are their last line of defence for getting penalised.
## Penalties, if this will ever come or if we accept them we need to consider the following:
### The trips that come to us are ‘higher risk’ trips since they are not addressed by Noot secured supply (would need to check whether these are mostly on-demand or scheduled)
### there should be a very clear definition of why Bolt (not Noot) should be penalised (this is effectively a penalty from Noot, not the municipality). In other words, we can accept getting penalised for things 100% attributable to our operation (not traffic, weather, changes in schedule, late notices, on-demand (when demand is high or supply is limited → higher contractual ETA) requests, etc)

Conclusion: 

* I wouldn’t like to see T&Cs adjusted in an ad-hoc basic without a clear commitment and security on overflow demand from their side → hence, becoming an official subcontractor of the contract with a secured volume of trips
* If we don’t have this security, why should we accept the penalties / risks for a contract we didn’t sign up for?

* _Cláusulas 10.ª e 13.ª – Responsabilizam a arrendatária apenas por danos imputáveis ou resultantes de negligência, o que, como já demonstrado, não se verifica._

# Privacy reviewed the DPA twice and shared its feedback with City Legal & business stakeholder. Details:

* *Security measures (Clause 3.2.3)* – City Legal refuses to reference Bolt’s Infosec standard. We requested City Legal’s own security measures for review.
** *Risk:* supplier’s measures may be weaker than Bolt’s standard requirements, increasing exposure to data breaches.
** *Action point*: Once provided, we advise to forward them to Infosec for review and approval - this is a necessary step if a supplier does not agree to reference our Infosec standard.
* *Data breach notification (Clause 3.2.6)* – based on current drafting, Bolt will only receive a short notification regarding an occurred data breach and then Bolt can request further details from the supplier if necessary. By standard, Bolt requires more comprehensive initial notification re/ the breach, which is required to meet our GDPR reporting obligations.
** *Risk:* Bolt could be unable to assess the breach as reportable and notify regulators on time, leading to compliance failures and potential fines.
* *Sub-processor notification (Clause 3.3(e))* – Wording may not give Bolt sufficient visibility or control over new sub-processors.
** *Risk:* While the practical risk is low, the clause limits Bolt’s ability to object effectively to sub-processors. Without receiving adequate details in the initial notification, Bolt may be unable to properly assess compliance risks before the sub-processor is engaged. This could result in reputational or regulatory exposure if unsuitable sub-processors are engaged by City Legal.

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Note on Liability Risk – City Legal*

City Legal confirmed they will not accept changes to the liability and indemnity allocation under the DPA, insisting on regulation through the general liability provisions in the main agreement. This is a risk business must accept if we proceed.

While the £3m liability cap is acceptable given the scope and value of services, the general liability clause in *Terms of Business* excludes carve-outs for data protection breaches. Key risks include:

* *Exclusion of indirect/consequential losses*: The clause excludes loss of data, reputational harm, loss of contracts, revenue, and goodwill—exactly the types of damage likely to result from a personal data breach.
{panel}

I’ve double checked the analysis of Polish local law + Polish privacy regulator’s (DPA) views + GDPR compliance bits.

{panel:bgColor=#ffebe6}
+*_In short - where’s the problem:_*+ 
{panel}

Allowing “always-on” ATR in Poland would almost certainly be viewed by the Polish DPA as covert, continuous audio monitoring an intrusive form of surveillance that the DPA has previously linked to intelligence or law-enforcement use only. Even if Bolt relies on legitimate interest (*_read:_* maintain the same functionality as now, maintain ATR as-is, without collecting opt-in consent), it’s highly contestable under local interpretation. Proceeding would create high enforcement risk and reputational exposure, especially given the ongoing EU investigation into ATR I mentioned.

The only realistic path is to keep ATR event-based and improve adoption through UX nudges, not automation. Any “auto-record all trips” design should be parked pending a broader LIA refresh and supervisory dialogue.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Poland-specific legal assessment*
{panel}

# *No special law enabling continuous recording (**_read:_* *I am looking for potential exceptions in PL law allowing us to do this)*
Poland’s 2018 Data Protection Act doesn’t modify GDPR, and there is no sectoral rule authorising private entities to capture continuous audio. Without such a legal basis, the feature hinges entirely on Bolt’s legitimate interest, which the Polish DPA treats narrowly for audio recording.
# *DPA’s stance: audio = exceptional, similar to surveillance*
In its precedents ([sobering station|https://uodo.gov.pl/pl/138/2449]; [pharmacy case|https://www.termedia.pl/mz/Nagrywanie-rozmow-w-aptekach-sa-wyniki-kontroli-UODO,56423.html]), the DPA deemed audio recording permissible only in extraordinary, legally defined contexts. Recording without participants’ awareness - even if security-driven - is seen as covert monitoring, incompatible with fairness and transparency under Articles 5(1)(a) and 13 GDPR.
# *Transparency conflict*
If ATR auto-activates and the rider isn’t clearly informed in real time + doesn’t have the ability to opt-out, Bolt risks breaching transparency duties. The DPA expects visible signage or clear notice where monitoring occurs - meaning “silent” activation by default would likely be unacceptable. This is something we already discussed with [~accountid:712020:ae7c369e-0fb6-428c-8e40-e7775c5bbebe] in the past, but product has not yet implemented this.

h4. 

From a Polish law standpoint, auto-enabled ATR is not defensible. The only sustainable strategy is to keep ATR strictly incident-based (i.e. as-is), reinforce transparency, and grow adoption through education (and not having it on by default).

Before answering, a little background on how the system works. When the first invoice is issued for the company, the Agent Fisc. Profile is attempted to be created. (We use Fonoa as our provider). If the onboarding is not successful, the state of Agent = suspended, and invoices are not attempted to be fiscalized.

# Here the onboarding is successful and Agent profile is created. All invoices are attempted to be issued with those . Changing VAT code on the Agent and reissuing invoices should technically fail (as it happenned in one of the examples), while if some bugs occur, we end up in situation with duplicate invoices or something else (since it’s a bug, hard to predict a behavior). If you have other cases, we can go through them as well. To sum up, The VAT and reg. code can be changed until the first invoice is issued.
# Here the onboarding failed, and once you fix the Agent Profile, all invoices are attempted to be fiscalized with the data from the Agent Profile (hence no reissue is needed). We will have the inconsistency here between the Billing Document data and the fiscalization data, but that’s not critical.

*Outcome of Legal Assessment:*
The external counsel confirmed that the overall legal position is strong. The extraordinary termination of the lease appears justified based on the _Nutzungsuntersagung_ issued by the local building authority due to serious fire safety deficiencies.

*Key Findings:*

* *Responsibility:* The landlord is responsible for the object-related fire protection.
* *Defect (Sachmangel):* The _Nutzungsuntersagung_ constitutes a substantial defect; rent reduction (Mietminderung) applies automatically from the date of the authority’s order (approx. March).
* *Damages (Schadensersatz):* Possible claims exist since the landlord culpably provided a defective rental object.
** Typical recoverable items: moving and storage costs, expenses for replacement space, and operational losses directly linked to the unusable premises.
* *Prospects:* Counsel (Christian) considers the chances of success, including in court, as *very positive*. However, expectations regarding the *extent of recoverable damages* should remain realistic.

Hi [~accountid:712020:8a510079-f35e-41ce-8bd4-2649e41767cb] , apologies for the delay. For some reason I missed your msg in the ticket. 

Please find below legal review and suggestions:

*1. Contract structure and Version Control*

*Current position:*
Zellis may unilaterally update linked documents (Service Description Guide, Fair Use Policy, Sub-processor List) and these take precedence over the T&Cs.

*Risk:*
Bolt could become bound by new commercial, operational or data-processing terms introduced without consent.

*Required amendment:*

* Fix all referenced documents to the versions in effect at the contract start date.
* Any update to hyperlinked or external documents should be valid only if agreed in writing through formal Change Control.
* Insert clause confirming that, in case of conflict, the *signed T&Cs* prevail.

*2. Termination and Suspension*

*Current position:*
Termination is only allowed for material breach or insolvency. Zellis can suspend services or terminate for delayed payment of undisputed sums.

*Risk:*
Bolt cannot terminate for convenience or for persistent poor service. Payroll or pension processing could be suspended during a payment dispute.

*Required amendment:*

* Add *termination-for-convenience* on 60–90 days’ notice after the initial term.
* Add right to terminate for *repeated SLA breaches* (e.g. three consecutive months below threshold).
* Prohibit suspension of critical payroll/pension services while a good-faith payment dispute is unresolved.

*3. Pricing and Change Control*

*Current position:*
Automatic annual increase of RPI + 3%. Many operational changes are treated as chargeable at Zellis’s “standard rates.”

*Risk:*
Uncapped inflationary increases and unpredictable extra charges for ordinary process adjustments or legislative changes.

*Required amendment:*

* Cap increases at the lower of *3% or RPI*, with 60 days’ written notice.
* Define “Chargeable Change” narrowly; exclude legally required or minor configuration updates.
* Require Bolt’s *written pre-approval* for any additional cost over a defined threshold (e.g. £1,000).
* Include a *fixed-fee regime for statutory or legislative changes*.

*4. Service Levels and Remedies*

*Current position:*
Service credits are capped at 50% of monthly fees and are the sole financial remedy.

*Risk:*
Remedies are insufficient for large-scale errors affecting thousands of drivers.

*Required amendment:*

* Service credits to be *non-exclusive* (without prejudice to other remedies).
* Add express right to terminate for repeated SLA failures.
* Require monthly SLA reporting and quarterly service-review meetings as contractual obligations.

*5. Liability Cap and Indemnities*

*Current position:*
Liability capped at fees paid in previous 12 months; excludes indirect and data-related losses. Only an IP infringement indemnity exists.

*Risk:*
Potential exposure from payroll or data-processing errors could be far greater than this cap.

*Required amendment:*

* Increase Zellis’s liability cap to 2x annual fees or £2 million, whichever is higher.
* Add specific indemnities covering:
** Payroll and pension administration errors;
** Breach of data-protection or security obligations;
** Failure to meet regulatory filing or reporting obligations (HMRC/TPR).
* Require Zellis to maintain appropriate professional indemnity and cyber insurance (minimum £2 million).

*6. Scope and Regulatory Alignment*

*Current position:*
Services are defined for “*employees*” under a traditional payroll model.

*Risk:*
The documentation does not reflect that drivers are self-employed. 

*Required amendment:*

* Insert clause acknowledging that:
** The population covered comprises *self-employed drivers*;
** Zellis provides purely *administrative support* under Bolt’s instructions;
** The agreement does not create an employment relationship between Bolt, Zellis, or the drivers.
* Clarify that Bolt remains the “client” but not the “employer” for the purposes of data processing and pension legislation.
* Specify that Zellis must perform its services in compliance with the *Pensions Act 2008* and related automatic-enrolment regulations.
* Require Zellis to maintain systems capable of supporting *non-employee auto-enrolment* (irregular earnings, multiple engagements, opt-outs, re-enrolments).

*8. TUPE and Employment References*

*Current position:*
Standard TUPE clauses and HR administration references to “employees.”

*Risk:*
Could be used to imply an employment relationship, increasing reclassification risk.

*Required amendment:*

* Delete or expressly disapply TUPE provisions and all employment-related clauses.
* Insert “no employment relationship” confirmation.

*9. Audit and Governance*

*Current position:*
Audit rights are limited to those defined in the Service Schedule; governance reviews are described as optional.

*Risk:*
Insufficient transparency or ability to verify compliance or data handling at scale.

*Required amendment:*

* Include a right for Bolt or its appointed auditor to conduct *one annual audit* (or on reasonable suspicion) of Zellis’s performance, security, and compliance processes.
* Make monthly operational reviews and quarterly business reviews *mandatory* contractual obligations, with agreed actions recorded in writing.



*Summary - the biggest risks* 

# *Liability and Indemnities*
#* Liability capped at one year’s fees; no indemnity for data breaches, payroll errors, or regulatory failures.
#* A system failure could expose Bolt to millions in unrecoverable costs.
#*Action:* Increase the cap to at least two times annual fees or £2 million and include explicit indemnities for data, payroll, and compliance errors.
# *Unilateral Control of Terms and Subprocessors*
#* Zellis can amend linked documents and subprocessor lists unilaterally.
#* This undermines Bolt’s ability to manage contractual and compliance obligations.
#*Action:* Fix all referenced documents to the signed version and require written agreement for any future updates or new subprocessors.
# *Weak Service-Level Protection*
#* Service credits are capped at 50 % of fees and are the sole remedy.
#* There are no clear accuracy or timeliness standards for large-volume auto-enrolment.
#*Action:* Add driver-specific KPIs (enrolment accuracy, contribution timeliness, incident response), make credits non-exclusive, and allow termination for repeated under-performance.

* We resolved duplicate entries in the delivery-pricing-courier DB caused by cross-shard remote-config calls.

* *Root cause:* Admin Panel requests to remote-config were *randomly hitting different shards*, leading to cross-shard writes and duplicates.
** Traced Admin Panel API traffic and confirmed random shard selection.
** Raised [+a ticket+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C049U1GKWQN/p1760073920203479] with *PINT Support* describing the shard-routing issue.
** Implemented a temporary, routing workaround and deployed the changes.
* All live courier multiplier changes are now *synchronized* between Remote Config and the delivery-pricing-courier service DB across shards.
* We will replace the temporary workaround with a permanent fix once PINT addresses the routing problem.

*In Progress* - Migrate data from remote config to delivery-pricing-courier:
** We are migrating live courier earning multipliers from *Remote Config* to dedicated service endpoints to enable full CRUD operations through the *Admin Panel* and *Internal API*.
** Backend (In Review):
*** Implemented *four new Admin Panel endpoints* with appropriate VIEW/EDIT permissions.
*** Introduced the *CourierEarningLiveMultipliersService* to manage business logic and support upsert (insert/update) operations.
*** Enhanced the *repository layer* to support JSON serialization and atomic updates.
*** Updated *Internal API integrations* to route through the new service layer.
** Admin Panel:
*** Developing a *migration view* to transfer all existing city and zone multipliers from Remote Config to the delivery-pricing-courier service.
*** Updating the Admin Panel to *use the delivery-pricing-courier database* as the new data source for all multiplier CRUD operations.
** Goal: This migration will fully decouple multiplier management from Remote Config, solving the prerequisite for scheduled multipliers.

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] with the correct user ID 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt or previous failed payment that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments

Hello Team!

I completely understand why this might look like a double charge, but I can assure you that the user was only charged once. This is a common part of how card payments are processed. Here's what happens:

# When the user first makes a payment, the bank temporarily ‘reserves' the funds and this is just the bank setting aside the amount for the transaction. The user’s account balance might show less amount but the payment hasn’t actually been taken out by the bank yet.
# Later, when the payment is fully processed, that reserved amount is now “officially” debited from the user’s account. At that point, some banks send a second notification, which can make it seem like a second charge.


The refund is successfully completed. I would advise the user to check their final account balance or statement, where they can confirm that only one payment was actually withdrawn. The earlier “pending” amount will either drop off or convert into the final charge.

Cheers,
Afiba

# When the user first makes a payment, the bank temporarily ‘reserves' the funds and this is just the bank setting aside the amount for the transaction. The user’s account balance might show less amount but the payment hasn’t actually been taken out by the bank yet.
# Later, when the payment is fully processed, that reserved amount is now “officially” debited from the user’s account. At that point, some banks send a second notification, which can make it seem like a second charge.


I would advise the user to check their final account balance or statement, where they can confirm that only one payment was actually withdrawn. The earlier “pending” amount will either drop off or convert into the final charge.

Cheers,
Afiba

)
SELECT

currency,
payment_order_id AS last_payment_order_id,
adjusted_amount AS last_adjusted_amount,

FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
)

spd.currency,
spd.last_payment_row_created,
'https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/' || CAST(spd.last_payment_order_id AS varchar) AS last_payment_link,
ROUND(spd.last_adjusted_amount*1.00/r.rate,2) * -1 AS authorized_debt_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(co.uncovered_amount*1.00/r.rate),2),0) AS sum_uncovered_eur_before_auth
FROM successful_preauths_with_debt spd 
JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co ON spd.user_id = co.user_id AND spd.currency = co.price_currency
LEFT JOIN ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(spd.last_payment_row_created) AND r.currency = spd.currency
WHERE co.created_date BETWEEN date '2025-01-01' AND date '2025-08-31'
AND co.created < spd.last_payment_row_created
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
) AS x
WHERE x.authorized_debt_eur >= x.sum_uncovered_eur_before_auth
AND x.sum_uncovered_eur_before_auth > 0
GROUP BY 1 
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

Overview of the tools that we have already reviewed:

*VelocityEHS*

VelocityEHS integrates several AI-driven capabilities within its platform, reflecting a progressive approach to digital safety management. However, these AI tools do not fully align with the practical needs of safety event reporting. Key functionalities — such as AI-assisted corrective action generation, automatic translation and language detection, or seamless integration with communication tools like Slack — are either missing or underdeveloped. As a result, while VelocityEHS demonstrates potential through its AI initiatives, it currently falls short of delivering targeted, efficiency-enhancing solutions that would truly support modern, multilingual, and collaborative safety management environments.


*Benchmark*

Benchmark presents a robust feature set, but the platform’s overall usability remains a significant challenge. Its interface is highly complex, making navigation and task execution cumbersome for both new and experienced users. The system is neither intuitive nor particularly user-friendly, which may hinder consistent engagement and reporting accuracy. Although Benchmark incorporates certain AI integrations, their performance currently falls short of expectations — offering limited practical value in supporting event analysis or automating corrective actions.

*Quentic*

Followed up with *Public Policy (*[*@marc.naether*|https://bolt.enterprise.slack.com/team/U02JG3SLFU7]*)*, we’ve confirmed the situation as follows:

Under Dutch law (Regeling maximumtarief en bekendmaking tarieven taxivervoer, artikel 1c), every *_vervoersbewijs (trip receipt)_* must include certain mandatory fields, even those that can be privacy sensitive, such as the *address* and *phone number of the operator (driver)*.

Normally, an *_invoice_* *(**_factuur_**)* is a separate document that may deviate from this format, but *Bolt combines both  the trip receipt and the invoice into one document.* Because of that, *all legally required fields of the vervoersbewijs must appear on the Bolt invoice* to ensure compliance.

So in any case the rider should receive a document with all privacy sensitive fields.

*Mitigation for driver privacy and safety*
[@nl-cs|https://bolt.enterprise.slack.com/admin/user_groups] to communicate with worried driver to limit exposure of personal data, drivers (especially independent ones) by:

* Using a *separate work phone number* instead of a private number.
* Register a *postbusadres (P.O. box)* or *business address via KVK* instead of their home address.
* If applicable, *fleet operators’ details* (address and phone) will be used for rides completed under their company.

*FYI from IBFD 9 October* 

Tax Authorities Publish First Set of Guidelines on Pillar Two Legislation

The tax authorities have published a first set of guidelines commenting on the French legislation implementing the global minimum level of taxation for multinational and large-scale domestic groups (GloBE rules) which is codified under articles 223 VJ et seq. of the General Tax Code (_Code général des impôts_, CGI).

The guidelines were published under a new section entirely dedicated to the global minimum tax ([+BOI-IMG+|https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14736-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IMG-20251008]). They summarize the applicable legislation and provide clarifications and examples derived from the OECD GloBE Commentary.

The first set of guidelines provide clarifications regarding:

|–    |definitions applicable to the GloBE rules ([+BOI-IMG-DEF+|https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14738-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IMG-DEF-20251008]); and|
|–    |the scope and territoriality rules ([+BOI-IMG-CHAMP+|https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14737-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IMG-CHAMP-20251008]), with three subdivisions regarding entities within the scope of Pillar Two rules ([+BOI-IMG-CHAMP-10+|https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14733-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IMG-CHAMP-10-20251008]), excluded entities ([+BOI-IMG-CHAMP-20+|https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14751-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IMG-CHAMP-20-20251008]), and territoriality rules ([+BOI-IMG-CHAMP-30+|https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14751-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IMG-CHAMP-20-20251008]).|

The tax authorities also announced future guidelines (currently being drafted) regarding:

|–    |safe harbours (BOI-IMG-RP);|
|–    |the effective tax rate (BOI-IMG-TEI);|
|–    |the calculation of the top-up tax (BOI-IMG-LIQ);|
|–    |the taxpayer and top-up tax payment rules (BOI-IMG-RED);|
|–    |rules on groups and reorganizations (BOI-IMG-REORG);|
|–    |specific regimes (BOI-IMG-PART);|
|–    |transitory rules applicable when MNEs enter the scope of the GloBE rules (BOI-IMG-TRANS);|
|–    |filing and payment obligations (BOI-IMG-DECLA); and|
|–    |collection, auditing and dispute rules (BOI-IMG-PROCD).|

The guidelines are accessible [+here+|https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14752-PGP.html/ACTU-2025-00122] (in French only).

The tax authorities published the guidelines on 8 October 2025.

** What exactly will these partners do with the driver data? *If Bolt contacts drivers directly, we risk antagonizing fleets. ** Will they be listed as third-party offers within Bolt Rewards only, or will they actively reach out to drivers? *They will be listed as third-party partners within Bolt Rewards. Our outsource agency will reach out to drivers.* 
** If they reach out, will the calls be positioned as coming from Bolt or directly from the accounting partners? *From outsource centers calling in the name of accounting companies*
* *Comparison with Romania*
** In Romania, partners contacted drivers directly by phone. That triggered GDPR marketing rules and required us to collect explicit opt-in consent before sharing driver contact details.
** Please clarify if Croatia intends to follow the same setup, or if it will differ (e.g. only in-app listing, no outbound calls). *We want to have same setup as Romania - outbound calls to drivers informing them about benefits of self-employment and how can easily been done by agencies doing all paperwork for them*

** Understanding the necessity and purpose for each data field is key for the DSA and privacy notice updates.
* *Role of the two partners*
* Are both agencies offering the same services, or do they have distinct roles in the program?

*Role of accounting companies for drivers is the same and it is as follows:*

* *Setting up driver businesses*
* *Obtaining required licenses*
* *Providing accounting support*
* *Ensuring business-related obligations (VAT, licenses, etc.) are paid regularly and on time*
* *Controlling company spend (in case of LLC)*

Advise the customer to *check with their bank* to confirm the release of the preauthorisation. Banks handle these releases differently, and while some are immediate, others may process it as a temporary charge that is then refunded. The reversal can take up to *30 days* to complete, as pending authorisations typically expire after that time on banks end.

Unfortunately, we don't have full visibility into all the parties involved in the payment processing beyond our payment partner. Therefore, we can't track the exact status of the preauthorisation release once it has been sent.

_The procedure for notifying the Personal Data Protection Committee (PDPC) of a DPO appointment remains largely unchanged based on our research. _Again, there isn't any published guidance which expressly addresses this question directly, but our understanding is that a DPO is likely to be considered officially appointed once:_

* _the organisation has formally designated the DPO internally (by letter of appointment, for example); and_
* _the PDPC has been notified using the prescribed form; and_

From a data protection POV, there is no legal ground to share such information, and the rider’s name (or any information concerning them) cannot be disclosed to the driver’s legal representative. Under the GDPR, this constitutes personal data of a third party, and disclosing it without a lawful basis would infringe their rights and freedoms. A private lawyer’s request does not provide a sufficient legal ground for such disclosure. Bolt may share this information only if required by a competent authority in the context of formal legal proceedings.

You may include the following paragraph in your answer to the legal rep:

{quote}From a data protection standpoint, Bolt is unable to disclose the name or any identifying information of the person involved in the report. This information constitutes personal data of a third party, and sharing it without a lawful basis would infringe their rights and freedoms under the General Data Protection Regulation. A request from a legal representative does not in itself establish a valid legal ground for disclosure. +*BACKGROUND*+

* Bolt is partnering with Lidl (Poland), transaction value of 10,000. Governed by this agreement: [Link|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IsriVkpeyEUTL-X4YipGni345MtcXND_/edit]
** Lidl offers its customers a loyalty program (Lidl Plus'). Under this programme, customers on the Lidl app can access promotional offers. This partnership governs Bolt offering discounted services to Lidl customers (apparently Bolt is offering this directly to Lidl customers).
* Under the partnership, Bolt must provide Lidl with discount codes, which Lidl shall make available to its customers (it appears that at the time of sharing, these are not yet connected to an individual. This becomes the case once shared).
** Bolt must also provide Lidl with monthly KPI results (i.e., number of users, value of transactions etc.).
* Clauses 5.6 - 5.9 contains data protection provisions.
** 5.6 - Bolt parties agree to provide Article 14 GDPR language. Fine.
** 5.7 - Parties agree to comply with GDPR. Fine.
** 5.8 - “The Parties declare that no personal data will be processed under the Agreement and the Parties will not entrust each other with the processing of personal data” - This is fine, {color:#4c9aff}if it is true{color}.
** 5.9 - If Bolt eventually decides to share personal data with Lidl, a DPA must be concluded “under pain of losing the right to seek liability from Lidl for violations of law or third-party rights”. If Bolt does not, Bolt releases Lidl from any liability, and will cover any damages for data protection violations. {color:#ff5630}We cannot accept the second part of the provision{color}.
*** If found in breach, Bolt owes Lidl 70,000 zloty (£14,000)
* Regional Legal has made liability mutual, and removed Lidl’s liability cap. No obvious indemnities.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* If we are not sharing any personal data with Lidl, there is no issue here. We just need to make sure the agreement is appropriately future-proofed - this is where clause 5.9 comes into play.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Questions:
** Who is marketing this to Lidl customers - Lidl or Bolt? (Should be the former)
** Am I correct in understanding that we are only sharing the codes, and they are not yet linked to individuals?
* Otherwise, not much to advise on here for now.

We evaluated the option to have 1 learning plan per vertical per market (eg. RH Onboarding Thailand). This would be a great way to ensure an agent is enrolled in all courses applicable to them from the start without having to self-enrol in any courses. 

Some problems came up: 

* Scalability → This seems like a good option now but can easily result in >100 learning plans 
* Duplication → Every learning plan for 1 vertical consists of 90% same content. There is no option to duplicate learning plans in Docebo, so a training specialist would have to manually assign all courses to a new LP each time 
* Learning Plan visibility → Learning plans cannot be assigned to Power Users in bulk. If you create a new learning plan, you need to manually assign it to each PowerUser, across all BPOs. This isn’t manageable long term. 

Alternative solution: 

* 1 global vertical onboarding learning plan & up-skill learning plan
* 1 market specific learning plan, either per vertical or including all verticals

This option still leads to many learning plans but allows us to: 

* Manage global enrolment & reporting on Onboarding & up-skill 
* Local management & reporting of learning plans for market specifics

{quote}_From slack:_
[~accountid:712020:209f6e12-e421-4fbf-9a9f-60d100117bab] _Do you feel strongly about calling it a booking fee, or is it more of a preference rather than a material legal risk if we go with reservation fee instead? My initial concern was that it might get confused with the standard booking fee we charge on the principal model for all trips, not just the scheduled ones._{quote}

There’s scope to tell the business it can use ‘reservation fee’ if it prefers, but it should be an informed choice, given that this wording may increase the risk of complaints.

It’s not clear what is actually being ‘reserved’, since we don’t guarantee that any driver will accept the order. When booking a scheduled ride, the app states: _“_*_Please note, Bolt cannot guarantee that a driver will confirm your trip request or fulfil your order._*_”_ A picky customer could easily raise an issue, for instance after missing a flight. In such cases, it may be difficult to identify what service the ‘reservation fee’ was paid for, noting that disclaimer.

As a result, compared to other options:

* calling it a ‘reservation fee’ may increase the likelihood of passenger complaints; and
* refunding the fee might not be seen as adequate compensation by customers or regulators.

For these reasons, ‘*_Advanced Booking_* *Fee*’ may be more suitable as it avoids conflict with the disclaimer.

Alternatively, the team could increase the existing ‘Service Fee’ for scheduled rides and require it to be paid upfront, rather than introducing a new fee altogether.

Regardless, to enable the business to make the decision it wants to make, you can tell them:

* it can mitigate the risks by doing its best to ensure that a driver is available and that rides are not cancelled, for example by offering an attractive price, and
* it can choose to deal with complaints if and when they arise, and we can pivot to alternative wording later if needed.

As for any overlap with Black Cabs definitions, it is not necessarily problematic since Parts 2 and 3 of the terms have separate definitions. Still, you could make aesthetic differences to distinguish them, for example by using ‘Black Cabs Booking Fee’.

* {{form-data}} v2.3.2 → [already fixed|https://github.com/form-data/form-data/issues/563] in [v4.0.1|https://github.com/form-data/form-data/releases/tag/v4.0.1], should upgrade to latest [v4.0.4|https://github.com/form-data/form-data/releases/tag/v4.0.4]
* {{@kafkajs/confluent-schema-registry}} v2.0.1 depends on {{protobufjs}} v6.11.4 → should upgrade to {{@kafkajs/confluent-schema-registry}} v3.9.0, which depends on {{protobufjs}} v7.4.0, which contains no more {{util.isArray}} references

{{bolt-server}} dependencies:

* {{form-data}} v3.0.0 → [already fixed|https://github.com/form-data/form-data/issues/563] in [v4.0.1|https://github.com/form-data/form-data/releases/tag/v4.0.1], should upgrade to latest [v4.0.4|https://github.com/form-data/form-data/releases/tag/v4.0.4]
* {{onlinepayments-sdk-nodejs}} v4.19.0 → should upgrade to latest [v6.2.0|https://github.com/wl-online-payments-direct/sdk-nodejs/releases/tag/6.2.0], contains no references to {{util.isArray}}
* {{@kafkajs/confluent-schema-registry}} v2.0.0 depends on {{protobufjs}} v6.11.4 → should upgrade to {{@kafkajs/confluent-schema-registry}} v3.9.0, which depends on {{protobufjs}} v7.4.0, which contains no more {{util.isArray}} references
* {{mixpanel}} v0.17.0 → 🚫 [https://github.com/mixpanel/mixpanel-node|https://github.com/mixpanel/mixpanel-node|smart-link] still uses {{util.isArray}}, {color:#ff5630}*either replace the library or fix it upstream*{color}
affected backend components:
** {{./src/rides/driver/driverx_events/main}}
** {{./src/platform/comms/event/main}}
* {{jsdom}} v20.0.1 depends on {{form-data}} v4.0.0 → should upgrade to latest [v27.0.0|https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/releases/tag/27.0.0], does not depend on {{form-data}} anymore
* {{@slack/web-api}} v6.8.1 depends on on {{form-data}} v2.5.0 → should upgrade to latest [v7.11.0|https://github.com/slackapi/node-slack-sdk/releases/tag/%40slack%2Fweb-api%407.11.0], depends on {{form-data}} v4.0.4 (deprecated references fixed)

[~accountid:630e0b9a9796033b256bd3a5] Thank you for reporting the issue. At a superficial look the issue seems trivial, but actually it’s quite serious because {{util.isArray}} will be removed in the next node.js major version and would break all dependencies still using the deprecated function. There are plans to attempt a node v22->v24 upgrade soon, so this literally blocks the upgrade.

To make matters worse, there’s a dependency (your component doesn’t depend on it) that _cannot simply be upgraded_ because its authors didn’t bother to replace {{util.isArray}} with {{Array.isArray}}. It’s gonna be loads of fun to patch it in upstream and, although the effort will be small, it’s gonna take a long time to fix and upgrade that dependency.

So you might have saved PINT from some serious head ache by reporting this minor annoyance with the warning.

h3. ## 2. Incorrect I2S and Analog Input Wiring (Critical Failure)



The digital audio data input pin ({{DIN}}) is incorrectly wired.

* *The Problem:* The digital audio data input pin, {{DIN}} (pin 13), appears to be connected to the analog input pin, {{AINL}} (pin 4), and left floating. The audio source from the processor, {{I2S_DOUT}}, is incorrectly connected to the codec's data *output* pin {{GPIO/DOUT}} (pin 18).
* *Why It's a Problem:* The codec will not receive any digital audio data to play. Connecting a digital pin to an analog pin is nonsensical and will not work. The processor's Data Out should go to the codec's Data In.
* *The Fix:*
*# Disconnect the {{I2S_DOUT}} net from pin 18 ({{GPIO/DOUT}}).
*# Connect the {{I2S_DOUT}} net to pin 13 ({{DIN}}).
*# If the analog inputs ({{AINL}}, {{AINR}}) are not used, they should be terminated according to the datasheet recommendations (typically grounded through a capacitor).

Hi Simon, 

To get back to you on this and to break down the legal and regulatory framework that governs taxi: 

* Taxis and PHVs are subject to distinct regulatory regimes, each requiring separate authorisations and documentation. Drivers cannot switch between the two without meeting the specific requirements of each. This legal incompatibility (unless both sets of authorisations are held) is clearly stated in [Article 3122-1 of the Code of Transport|https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000029532146/2015-01-01 ].
* With regards to having a merged “standard” category which includes taxis and PHVs - I think that this is possible once we launch the Fixed Price for Taxis and that Bolt covers the difference in the fare. 
* As discussed, I would recommend talking to Louis and Mathilde about the “All Cars” Category that they want to launch which could includes taxis at a fare price.



To respond specifically to the pricing questions:

* A taxi driver cannot legally perform PHV (VTC) activities without holding the appropriate VTC certification. If the driver only holds a taxi licence, the taximeter must apply, and the ride must comply with taxi fare regulations.



So to answer your questions, where a driver has the dual licence (Taxi + VTC), then yes, they could exercise both activities, but they would have to segregate the two activities:

* *Taxi rides* must follow the taxi pricing regime (horokilometric fare) and use the taximeter.
* *VTC rides* must comply with the rules applicable to VTCs, including pricing and reservations, and avoid street pick-ups.



*Practical Considerations*

* It’s legally feasible but administratively burdensome, as the driver must comply with both regimes.
* The vehicle used may need to be adapted or dual-equipped if switching roles.



Happy to discuss further to clarify any of the points above ! 

Thanks

Hi [~accountid:6052892160d39e006f72f166], 

Thank you for your patience on this ticket. 

To respond to your query, please note that under French law, the use of foreign license plates by professional drivers (e.g., taxi or PHV) *is not permitted for long-term operation*. The relevant rules require that:

# Vehicles must be registered in France if used by a professional driver operating regularly in France.
# A French registration (immatriculation) is essential for:
#* Ensuring proper insurance coverage;
#* Accessing certain regulatory frameworks, including VTC licensing and parking permits for taxis;
#* Ensuring compliance with vehicle safety inspections under French standards.



*Rentals with foreign plates →* if the vehicles are *rentals and cannot be re-registered in France*, *they cannot be legally used for providing transport services in France*, including via Bolt’s platform. These vehicles do not meet the requirements for professional transport use and risk fines or impoundment if detected by authorities.



*Recommendation*

A short term tolerance may be applied if they are in the process of being re-registered in France. 

However, you should *not authorize continued operation* of foreign-registered vehicles beyond the one-month transition period, unless:

WITH has_keep_preauth_check AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
a.meta.order_id,
a.meta.city_id
FROM archive_analytical.rides_payment_capture_authorized_amount a
WHERE a.created_hour BETWEEN date '2025-04-01' AND date '2025-06-30'
)
SELECT 
month(co.created) AS MONTH,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.card_booked_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS sum_booked_amount_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM((co.user_price - co.booking_amount_total)*1.00/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS sum_price_increase_that_goes_to_debt,
SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS sum_user_price_eur,
COUNT(DISTINCT co.id) AS count_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.initial_failed_payment_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS initial_fp_sum,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS fp_sum,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) - ROUND(CAST(SUM((co.user_price - co.booking_amount_total)*1.00/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS opportunity
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
JOIN has_keep_preauth_check kpc ON kpc.order_id = co.order_id AND kpc.city_id = co.city_id

AND co.is_current_failed_payment 
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC

*Draft Response:*

Dear Sir ,

Thank you for reaching out to share your concerns regarding the presence and working conditions of private hire drivers on the Côte d’Azur.

We acknowledge the issues raised in your message and appreciate the opportunity to clarify Bolt’s role and responsibilities as a platform operating in France.

Bolt is a licensed booking platform (_centrale de réservation_) operating under French law. We comply fully with all legal obligations, including verifying that each driver holds a valid driving licence, professional card, civil liability insurance, and vehicle insurance before their first trip, and at least annually thereafter. We reject any driver who does not meet these requirements.

We do not organize or manage how drivers structure their working hours or accommodation. However, for safety reasons, and in order to reduce the risk of fatigue-related road accidents, we may in limited cases suspend access to the app when a driver has provided services for more than 10 consecutive hours.

Also, we recognize that traffic can be a concern during the high season. However, professional VTC drivers are subject to national licensing and qualification requirements. All drivers on our platform must be individually verified, and our systems are not open to unvetted use. 

With regard to the reference to “Arrêté préfectoral n° 2025-101 / 2025,” we are not aware of any such official order. If it were to be issued, we would of course review it and ensure full compliance.

We also understand that your message may have been shared with media outlets. Bolt welcomes fact-based public discussion and remains open to constructive engagement with both the press and public authorities.

We are committed to operating responsibly, in full compliance with French law, and to treating all transport professionals who use our technology with fairness and transparency. If you have details of a specific issue involving a Bolt driver, please do share them with us via our support channels so we can follow up accordingly.

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

{code:sql}WITH conferences_with_duration AS (
    SELECT
        conference_id,
        MAX(duration) AS duration
    FROM
        ng_customer_support.voip_conference_call_event
    WHERE
        caller_type = 'support' AND
        created_date >= date '2025-09-01' AND
        created_date < date '2025-10-01' AND
        type = 'dice' AND
        result = 'ANSWERED'
    GROUP BY
        conference_id
    HAVING
        MAX(duration) > 1
), conferences_with_recording AS (
    SELECT
        DISTINCT conference_id
    FROM
        ng_customer_support.voip_conference_call_event
    WHERE
        type = 'notify:recording_finished' AND
        created_date >= date '2025-09-01' AND
        created_date < date '2025-10-02'
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS count
FROM
    conferences_with_duration AS cwd
LEFT JOIN
    conferences_with_recording AS cwr
ON
    cwd.conference_id = cwr.conference_id
WHERE
    cwr.conference_id IS NULL
;{code}

* Wait 1-2 mins
* restart the app
* Check app requests - "driver/v2/getWorkingTimeInfo"

For cases where refund was issued but can’t be seen on the user’s card or Bolt balance.

* Check where the refund was sent to and if it was successful on the [transaction history page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A%2225%22%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22target_account_id%22%3A%2265766018%22%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] with the correct user ID 
** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt or previous failed payment that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

[~accountid:712020:726e5ea0-027c-4c31-a0fd-2c23b80dc56c] *FYI from IBFD (10 October 2025):*

Belgium

_Report from Dr René Offermanns, Principal Associate, IBFD_

Government Submits Bill to Amend Minimum Tax to Parliament Including Clarifications of Entities Subject to Tax, Filling Obligations, Representative Appointment

The government has submitted an amending draft bill to the Chamber of Representatives (_Kamer van volksvertegenwoordigers/Chambre de Réprésentants_) to amend the minimum tax law, which provides for a minimum effective tax rate of 15% for groups, both domestic and international, with combined financial revenues of more than EUR 750 million a year, and with either a parent company or a subsidiary situated in an EU Member State. The main changes of the bill are summarized below.

Group Entities

The amendment abolishes the provision of article 2(2) of the Law on the introduction of Minimum Tax (LoMT) that all group entities are established in Belgium are subject to the minimum tax. This change confirms that a joint filing system applies, not individual filings by each group company.

Notifications

All notifications concerning the tax will be made through an electronic protected platform of the tax administration.

Definitions

The amendments include the definition for joint ventures definitions of group entity and reporting group entity. Accordingly, the scope of joint ventures does not include:

|–    |an ultimate parent entity of an MNE group or a large domestic group that must apply the Income Inclusion Rule (IIR);|
|–    |an exempt entity; and|
|–    |an entity whose ownership interests are held directly through an excluded entity by the MNE group or large domestic group if one of the following conditions is met:
–    
the entity is operated solely or almost solely to hold assets or invest funds for the benefit of its investors;
–    
the entity performs activities that are ancillary to the activities of the excluded entity; or
–    
substantially all of its income is excluded from the calculation of qualifying income or loss;|
|–    |an entity held by an MNE group or a large domestic group consisting exclusively of excluded entities; or|
|–    |an affiliated party to a joint venture if that party is included in joint accounts, a PE whose principal entity is a joint venture or an ultimate parent company.|

Domestic Top-Up Tax

The domestic top-up tax applies to group entities established in Belgium, including joint ventures and affiliated parties. If more

group entities or joint ventures are subject to this tax, one joint assessment will be imposed. The domestic top-up tax will be due if the effective tax rate is below 15%.

Income Inclusion Rule (IIR)

Subject to the IIR are, with respect to their low-tax group entities that are stateless or established in another jurisdiction (i.e. not regarded as resident), as well as with respect to group entities and their low-tax group entities established in Belgium, the following group entities established in Belgium:

|–    |an ultimate parent entity;|
|–    |an intermediate parent entity owned by an ultimate parent entity established in a third country or by an ultimate parent entity established in a Member State of the European Union that is an excluded entity; and|
|–    |a partially owned parent entity.|

Undertaxed Profits Rule (UTPR)

The amendments clarify that this rule applies to group entities established in Belgium, excluding investment entities, where the ultimate parent entity of the MNE group to which those group entities belong:

|–    |is an excluded entity;|
|–    |is established in a third-country jurisdiction that does not apply a qualified IIR; or|
|–    |is established in a jurisdiction that, for the purposes of this law, is considered a low-tax jurisdiction.|

If more group entities are subject to the UTPR, a joint assessment will be imposed.

Holding Structures

The amendment clarifies that a parent entity that directly or indirectly holds an ownership interest in a joint venture or an affiliated party has to apply the IIR to its attributable share of the additional tax on that joint venture or affiliated party. The calculation of the additional levies for the joint venture and its affiliated parties will be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the LoMT as if they were group entities of a separate MNE group or large domestic group, or as if the joint venture were the ultimate parent entity of that group.

The top-up tax payable by the joint venture group is reduced by the portion attributable to each parent entity of the top-up tax of each member of the joint venture group. Remaining surcharge amounts are added to the total UTPR surcharge amount

Tax Assessment

The tax authorities may not impose a tax assessment within 6 months after the minimum tax return was filed.

Statute of Limitation Period

The statute of limitation period is 6 years from 1 January of the year that designates the assessment year for which the tax is due.

Joint-Filing

Joint filing becomes obligatory for group entities, joint ventures, or affiliated parties established in Belgium. If a joint-venture is part of two groups, the amount of tax due by the joint-venture is allocated pro rata to the groups based on the ownership percentage.

Taxable Period

The taxable period is equal to the reporting year. The assessment year is equal to:

|–    |the year following the year in which the reporting year ends, if the reporting year ends on 31 December; and|
|–    |the year after the year in which the reporting year ends, if the reporting year does not end on 31 December.|

Representative

Groups may appoint a representing company. Otherwise, the group will be represented by:

|–    |the ultimate parent entity established in Belgium;|
|–    |if there is no ultimate parent entity of the group established in Belgium, the parent entity established in Belgium that directly or indirectly holds an ownership interest in all such group entities or the joint ventures established in Belgium and the parties affiliated with the joint ventures; or|
|–    |the group entity or joint venture established in Belgium or the party affiliated with the joint venture, with the highest balance sheet total.|

The representative files and pays the assessments. The full text of bill DOC 56 1070/001 of 1 October 2025, submitted to the chamber of representatives on 9 October 2025, is available [+here+|https://www.dekamer.be/flwb/pdf/56/1070/56K1070001.pdf] (in Dutch and French).

GH Real Talent product, which is currently in closed beta and launching soon, will handle this directly in Greenhouse. But there are a few recommendations to handle provided by GH:

h3. 1. Preventing Test/Fake Applications

Ways the system can be used today:

# [Captcha on application|https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005448066-Invisible-reCAPTCHA] - We have this on our Greenhouse-hosted job boards. As you are using an Option5 API-driven job board, your developers can implement this form along with validation on certain fields before they are sent via the job API to Greenhouse. 
# [Application limits|https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/24412757660443-Set-application-limits-for-job-posts] - reviewing and adjusting these limits. The spam applications normally come in volumes, so having a limit on high application volumes will help catch this.
# Marking [application as SPAM|https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205094045-Mark-a-candidate-as-spam] in-app, essentially blocking future applications from this profile.



Additional fraud/spam detection coming with  Real Talent:

* Fraud - This feature would use a candidate’s phone number, email address, and IP address to identify potential risk factors through a third-party vendor. Leveraging these risk scores, customers can make more informed decisions about which candidates to move forward with. A recruiter would view these risk scores in the candidate profile and app review.
* Spam - This feature would provide a designated area within Greenhouse where organizations can list spam email domains and IP addresses, allowing affected applications to automatically be rejected and marked as spam.

h3. 2. Identifying the Source of These Applications

You can pull the required [source reports for all candidates|https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042740232-Essential-candidate-report] directly in app to identify the trends. The source will also be available directly on the candidate profile if you are looking one by one. If you have a list or a few examples you want GH to look into, submit them to our technical support team. As the setup mirrors Romania’s model, the key point is that outbound calls to drivers promoting accounting partners qualify as _marketing communications_ under GDPR. This means that prior opt-in consent is required before any driver contact details (name, phone, email) are shared with third-party partners for these calls. See more details below.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
h3. Data sharing and lawful basis (overview)
{panel}

* *Data shared:* name, phone number, and optionally email.
* *Purpose:* enabling accounting partners (Meta Mate d.o.o., Smart Lift d.o.o.) to contact drivers about self-employment setup and accounting services.
* *Lawful basis:* _consent_ (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR).
** The consent must be *freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous*.
** It must *explicitly cover* the sharing of contact data with third-party partners for this purpose.

No other lawful basis (e.g., legitimate interest or contract necessity) applies here due to the promotional and commercial nature of the outreach.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
h3. Consent collection
{panel}

* Drivers must *opt-in* before data is shared.
* Consent can be gathered via the existing *Bolt Rewards* in-app pop-up or banner (same as in Romania).
* Consent must not be bundled with other Rewards or operational consents.
* Drivers who decline or withdraw consent must *not be contacted*.

To sum up, the safest and most compliant approach is to treat this outreach as marketing and obtain clear, specific opt-in consent from drivers to share their data with third-party partners. The consent language must also clearly state that the driver’s data will be shared with third parties for the purposes of these services. The consent mechanism can be integrated within the app (e.g., an opt-in pop-up) or other direct channels, as long as it clearly conveys the nature of data sharing and the third-party partners involved. 

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*_Example text_*

*Hi [Driver’s Name],*

We’d like to inform you about a new opportunity to receive support for your business through one of our trusted partners. This service includes assistance with setting up your own business, obtaining necessary licenses, and accounting support. If you are interested in receiving these offers, please confirm your consent to share your information with our partners.

[Yes, I Consent] [No, I Do Not Consent]
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
h3. Partner contact and representation
{panel}

* The *outsource partner* may call drivers _on behalf of_ the accounting companies, not Bolt.
* Call scripts should avoid implying the call originates from Bolt. Example phrasing:
“I’m calling from [Outsourced Agency] on behalf of [Meta Mate / Smart Lift], partners in the Bolt Rewards programme.”
* Partners must maintain an *internal do-not-contact list* and respect opt-outs.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
h3. Documentation and contracts
{panel}

* Each accounting company must have a *Data Sharing Agreement (DSA)* with Bolt, identical in structure to the Romania DSAs.
** Scope: data types, purpose (partner offer), consent as lawful basis, deletion timelines.
** Include confidentiality, security, audit, and breach-notification clauses.
* The outsource agency acts as *Bolt’s processor* (contracted under Bolt’s standard DPA).

decided to check all PRs from a high-level perspective, looking at the pricing outcomes. what sort of actions we do. 

[^PRs pricing outcome.xlsx]

{code:sql}SELECT 
month(x.created) AS MONTH, 
x.pricing_outcome,
x.strategy_,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.orderlink,0.0041) AS count_PRs,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.orderlink, 0.0041) * 1.00/SUM(APPROX_DISTINCT(x.orderlink, 0.0041)) OVER (PARTITION BY month(x.created),x.strategy_) AS ratio_outcome,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.id IS NOT NULL THEN x.orderlink END,0.0041) AS count_refunds,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.id IS NOT NULL THEN x.orderlink END,0.0041) * 1.00/SUM(APPROX_DISTINCT(x.orderlink, 0.0041)) OVER (PARTITION BY month(x.created),x.strategy_,x.pricing_outcome) AS refund_ratio
FROM ( 
SELECT 
'https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/' || CAST(a.meta.order_id AS varchar) || '/' || CAST(a.meta.city_id AS varchar) AS orderlink,
a.created,
ROUND(CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.actual_info.price') AS REAL)*1.00,2) AS actual_price,
ot.ride_price AS final_order_price,
co.id,
b.name AS strategy_,
CASE 
	WHEN ot.ride_price = 0 THEN 'price_zero'
	WHEN ROUND(CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.actual_info.price') AS REAL)*1.00,2) = ROUND(CAST(ot.ride_price AS REAL)*1.00,2) THEN 'same_price'
	WHEN ROUND(CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.actual_info.price') AS REAL)*1.00,2) < ROUND(CAST(ot.ride_price AS REAL)*1.00,2) THEN 'price_increase'
	WHEN ROUND(CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.actual_info.price') AS REAL)*1.00,2) > ROUND(CAST(ot.ride_price AS REAL)*1.00,2) THEN 'price_decrease'
	ELSE 'other'
END AS pricing_outcome
FROM archive_analytical.driver_order_price_check a
CROSS JOIN UNNEST (a.strategies) AS b 
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON a.meta.order_id = ot.order_id AND a.meta.city_id = ot.city_id 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co ON a.meta.order_id = co.order_id AND a.meta.city_id = co.city_id AND co.order_type = 'rides' AND COALESCE(co.refund_amount,0) > 0 AND co.created_date >= date '2025-08-01'
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2025-08-01'
AND ot.created_date >= date '2025-08-01'
AND ot.state = 'finished'
AND a.decision.decision = 'review_needed'
) AS x
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2,1 DESC{code}

hi [~accountid:712020:d008dcec-6cfe-47e4-83a0-c29522744742] ,

I wanted to follow up with a quick clarification on the incompatibility between VTC and taxi driver status.

Based on my understanding, under Article R.3120-7 of the French Transport Code, the activity of taxi driving is incompatible with that of a VTC driver. So yes, *VTC and taxi activities are not legally compatible*.

That being said, in practice, *we have no way of verifying whether a driver has applied for and received both a VTC and taxi license*. If someone were registered under both categories simultaneously, unless we are notified or flagged by the authorities, *we wouldn’t necessarily be aware of this situation or its illegality*.

From a product perspective, however, it seems that dual registration is *not technically feasible*, primarily because drivers have to accept different sets of T&Cs. *The taxi and VTC onboarding flows are separate and tailored to each regime*, making it operationally difficult to register under both streams with the same account.

That’s my current take, but I suggest double-checking this with Aurélien and Xavier to confirm.

thanks,

Eli

From our side, the scale of the issue seems relatively limited, around 30 affected accounts out of roughly 9k business riders in Ghana (0.33%) within 1 year. Since these attacks rely on phishing, it’s unclear how enforcing MFA would change that behavior. If someone already shares their OTP, they’re just as likely to share the second factor too.

Given the limited impact and questionable effectiveness of this measure, we don’t see a strong enough reason to pick this up right now, but happy to revisit if data shows broader impact. It likely makes more sense to continue reinforcing proactive awareness campaigns around OTP sharing and account safety, since the current issue seems primarily social engineering-driven.
